name: Learn basic wood carving
blurb: Whittling with a single knife: grain reading, a handful of controlled cuts, and safe grips. Cheap, portable and genuinely meditative.
gear: A sharp carving knife with a fixed blade
A cut-resistant glove and a thumb guard
steps: Learn to sharpen and strop. A carving knife must be shaving sharp, and blunt tools are what cause slips and injuries.
Learn to read grain: cutting downhill with the grain slices cleanly, cutting against it tears and catches.
Learn the four core cuts: the push cut, the pull or paring cut, the thumb-pushing cut and the stop cut.
Learn safe body position — always cut away from your body, and know where the blade goes if it slips.
Carve simple projects: a wedge, a chain link, a small animal, a spoon blank.
Strop frequently while working rather than sharpening rarely.
tips: Wear the glove on the hand holding the wood. Almost all carving injuries land there.
If the knife is fighting you, you are cutting against the grain. Turn the wood around.
proof: A finished carved object with clean, unforced cuts and no tear-out.
